$comment: Hand-edited (docs/SCHEMA.md). The Northwestern Pacific's electric lines in Marin (Phase 2b.D). Research: docs/research/east-bay-electric.md, section 4.

lines.name: Sausalito–San Rafael electric line
lines.summary: Third-rail electric trains from the ferry at Sausalito by Mill Valley Junction, the Alto tunnel, Corte Madera, Larkspur, Ross and San Anselmo to San Rafael: the first third-rail line in California.
lines.fate_note: Service ended on March 1, 1941, along with the railroad's ferry, when its pooling arrangement with Pacific Greyhound was canceled (CRC Decision No. 34457).

sources.note: "the main line to San Rafael was opened on Oct. 17" (1903), "the first third-rail road to be constructed and put into operation in California".
"... discontinued all service on its interurban electric line between Sausalito and San Rafael" on March 1, 1941.

lines.notes: Run by the North Shore Railroad, which became part of the Northwestern Pacific; the date of the change isn't sourced here. Other routes (by Greenbrae, and on to Manor) aren't drawn.

lines.name: Mill Valley electric line
lines.summary: Third-rail electric trains from the ferry at Sausalito to Mill Valley, by the branch from Mill Valley Junction: the first of the North Shore's electric services.
lines.fate_note: Service ended on March 1, 1941, with the rest of the electric lines (CRC Decision No. 34457).

sources.note: "The Mill Valley branch of the new system was placed in operation on Aug. 21" (1903).
Decision No. 34457 names the line "between Sausalito and San Rafael"; that the Mill Valley trains ended with it is inferred, not stated.

lines.notes: Run by the North Shore Railroad, then the Northwestern Pacific. Decision No. 34457 names only the Sausalito-San Rafael line; the Mill Valley branch is taken to have ended with it.
